opener.seg: [Inclosure to inclosure in No. 222.—From the North China Daily News, September 8, 1892.]

div.p: We received yesterday the following telegram dated Singan Fu, 6th September, 6:30 p.m.: “European Missionary Christians mutilated Shensi,” which evidently means that there has been an anti-Christian outbreak in Shensi in which European missionaries and native Christians have been mutilated. The epidemics that have visited northern central China this year have, we know, been taken advantage of by the enitides of missionary work, and it is to be feared that these men have succeeded in stirring up a riot in Shensi. The China Inland Mission has 27 members, including associates, in Shensi, mostly in the west of the province, at Fengsiang, Hanchung, Chengku, and Sanyang. There are 30 Franciscans in Shensi, including 7 nuns, and many of these are near Singan Fu. There are also 3 English Baptist missionaries in the province. It is difficult to know what can be done to assist the foreigners in Shensi, if they need assistance, the nearest port being Hankow, but we understand that information of the trouble has been telegraphed to Sir John Walsham, who will no doubt make the necessary representations to the Chinese authorities.
